description:
**Official documentation and how-tos** — the pages you would hand to someone using Weave for the first time.

Prescriptive rather than exploratory: how to install it, how the data model works, what each field type does. Design rationale and open questions belong in **Wiki** instead.

tables.name: Guide
tables.description:
**Handbook pages** — the prescriptive documentation set.

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `Description` | The page body, in markdown |
| `Audience` | Who it is written for |
| `Order` | Reading sequence within the Handbook |

A guide should be safe to follow verbatim. If something is still being decided, it belongs in a Wiki article until it settles.

tables.name: Fields
tables.description:
**One page per field type** — the living reference for every field weave can make.

The storage primitives (`text`, `number`, `date`, `daterange`, `checkbox`, `url`, `email`), the choosers (`select`, `multiselect`, `workflow`), `relation` (always a bidirectional pair), the computed types (`lookup`, `rollup`, `formula`), `document`, and the three the meta-model earned: `field` (a value that IS a field definition), `key` (the name of a secret, never the secret) and `attachments`.

`Kind` groups them. Each page names every config key the vocabulary lists for its type, the closed set each key draws from, and what bites. `test/handbook.test.mjs` fails if a type ships without a page, or a page quotes a vocabulary the engine no longer has.

description:
**Design notes and architecture** — why Weave is shaped the way it is.

Where the Handbook says *how*, the Wiki says *why*: the trade-offs behind the storage layer, the reasoning behind the API surface, notes that are still being argued with. Content graduates to a Handbook guide once it stops changing.

tables.name: Article
tables.description:
**Wiki articles** — design notes, architecture write-ups and postmortems.

`Topic` groups them. Unlike Handbook guides these are allowed to be provisional: an article can argue a position, record a decision that was later reversed, or capture an investigation that went nowhere. That history is the point.

description:
**The Weave test suite, dogfooded** — the `node --test` run modelled as data.

One `Suite` per test file, one `Case` per test, with the suite's `Case Count` rollup kept equal to the real number of tests in that file. It exists to make coverage queryable and to make drift between the suite and reality visible instead of silent.

tables.name: Suite
tables.description:
**One row per test file.**

`File` is the path (`test/engine.test.mjs`), `Cases` links every test in it, and `Case Count` rolls those up. The rollup must equal the number of tests `node --test` actually reports for that file — a mismatch means either a test was added without a row, or a row outlived its test.

tables.name: Case
tables.description:
**One row per test**, linked to its `Suite`.

`Status` is a workflow: `Passing` (default), `Flaky`, `Failing`. Names are short labels for what the test pins down, not copies of the assertion. The value here is being able to ask "what covers this behaviour?" and get an answer.

description:
**Open issues and the roadmap**, maintained as Weave is built.

`Issue` is the defect log — anything found in use, including bugs fixed the same hour, so the history survives. `Feature` is the roadmap, grouped by milestone. Both are public: this is the space an outside contributor reads first.

tables.name: Issue
tables.description:
**The defect log.**

`Severity` is `Low` / `Medium` / `High`; `Status` runs `Open → In Progress → Fixed`. Bugs are logged even when they are fixed immediately — the record of what broke and why is worth more than the fix alone.

Rows are enriched by default: the report in the reporter's own words, a reproduction, the root cause, the fix, and the tests that now guard it. Screenshots and logs are attached as **copies** via the files API, never as a path to somewhere else.

tables.name: Feature
tables.description:
**The roadmap.**

`Milestone` groups the work; `Status` runs `Planned → In Progress → Shipped`. Shipped rows are kept rather than cleared — together they are the changelog, and the list of what has already been considered and decided.

tables.name: Release
tables.description: One row per release: version, date, landed commit, the Issues it fixes, the Features it ships, and the release notes as its Description. Notes are mandatory.

description: The workspace itself: its spaces and tables, as rows.

tables.name: Spaces
tables.description: Every space in this workspace, as a row. Creating a row creates the space; renaming it renames the space; hard-deleting it deletes the space and everything in it.

tables.name: Tables
tables.description: Every table in this workspace, as a row related to its space. Creating a row creates the table; renaming it renames the table; hard-deleting it deletes the table and its rows.

tables.name: Fields
tables.description: Every field of every table, as a row related to its table and carrying its definition. Creating a row creates the column; renaming it renames the column; editing its Definition changes the config; hard-deleting it deletes the column.

tables.name: Workflows
tables.description: Every workflow in this workspace, as a row: the tables and spaces it touches, its executable script, version, state, health, last run, and a mermaid diagram of itself.

tables.name: Workspaces
tables.description: Every workspace this weave serves, as a row: the hub root and every member workspace. Its spaces, tables, fields and workflows relate back to it. Workspaces are created and deleted from the hub, not as rows.

tables.name: Views
tables.description: Every view over every table, as a row related to its table: the columns it shows in order, its state filter and its sort. The first view of a table is its default. Creating a row creates the view; editing it edits the view; deleting it deletes the view.

description: What a field can be, and what a document can hold. `Field Types` puts every field type and several configurations of the same type side by side in one grid; `Formatting` gives every document construct a row written in the construct it names.

tables.name: People
tables.description: The rows the computed fields on `Field Types` hang off — a lookup, three rollups and two relations need somewhere to point.

tables.name: Field Types
tables.description: Every field type, and several configurations of the same type beside each other — number as plain, currency, percent and unit; date as iso, us and long with time; a coloured select beside a plain one; a full lifecycle beside a two-state gate; rollups by count, avg and join; numeric, text and date formulas; a flat and a nested field definition.

fields.name: Skill trend
fields.expression: if(empty([Peer skills]), null, sortby([Peer skills], [Peer joined]))

tables.name: Formatting
tables.description: Every construct a document can hold, each row written in the construct it names.

tables.name: Documents
tables.description: Every kind of document weave supports — one row per kind, each carrying a rich, real example

tables.name: Icons
tables.description: The icon vocabulary: where the set comes from, how a value is written, what moves and when. One row, kept canonical.

tables.name: Projects
tables.description: The workstreams every other Showcase row hangs off. A **target** in four of the polymorphic demos: [[table:Showcase/Notes]] `Related`, [[table:Showcase/Activity]] `Subject`, [[table:Showcase/Tags]] `Applied to`, and referenced from [[table:Showcase/Comments]] through their tasks. Plain table — the interesting fields live on the pointing side.

tables.name: Meetings
tables.description: Meetings are one of the three things a [[table:Showcase/Comments]] row can sit **on**, and one of the mixed set a [[table:Showcase/Tags]] row spans. Plain table with a date; the pointing fields live on Comments, Activity, Notes and Tags.

tables.name: Docs
tables.description: Documents that get commented on ([[table:Showcase/Comments]] `On`), tagged ([[table:Showcase/Tags]] `Applied to`) and cited from [[table:Showcase/Notes]] `Related`. Plain table with a `Kind`; the target-set fields point here from elsewhere.

tables.name: Notes
tables.description:
**WHY:** a note can be *about* a row **or about the structure that holds rows** — `Related` mixes [[table:Showcase/Projects]], [[table:Showcase/Meetings]] and [[table:Showcase/Docs]] rows with [[table:Workspace/Tables]] and [[table:Workspace/Spaces]] registry rows in one cell. Case 3 of the polymorphic showcase ([[Feature#182]]) and the walkthrough in Wiki article [[Article#5]]: because weave's tables and spaces are rows themselves, a relation can reach them. Migrated 2026-09-05 from the retired `showcase` workspace and extended.

`Related` → Projects | Meetings | Docs | Workspace/Tables | Workspace/Spaces, many-to-many.

tables.name: Tasks
tables.description: The busiest **target** in the set: a task takes comments ([[table:Showcase/Comments]] `On`), shows up in the audit log ([[table:Showcase/Activity]] `Subject`) and carries tags ([[table:Showcase/Tags]] `Applied to`). Each task belongs to one [[table:Showcase/Projects]] row through a classic paired relation — the counter-example to the polymorphic fields around it.

tables.name: Comments
tables.description:
**WHY:** a comment lives on anything — one `On` field that may point at a [[table:Showcase/Tasks]] row, a [[table:Showcase/Docs]] row or a [[table:Showcase/Meetings]] row, instead of three nullable relations of which exactly one is ever set. Case 1 of the polymorphic showcase (Feature [[Feature#182]]); the pattern behind the built-in comments, files and activity feeds.

`On` → Tasks | Docs | Meetings, many-to-one. The chip carries its home table so a reader can tell a task from a doc at a glance.

tables.name: Expenses
tables.description: Spend that needs a sign-off. One of the three subjects an [[table:Showcase/Approvals]] row can be **of**; also the single target of [[table:Showcase/Line Items]] `Expense` — the counter-example where a plain paired relation is right, because `Line total` rolls up through it.

tables.name: Contracts
tables.description: Agreements awaiting signature. One of the three subjects an [[table:Showcase/Approvals]] row can be **of** — a contract and an expense share nothing but the need for a decision, which is exactly when a target set beats a per-table approval field.

tables.name: Deploys
tables.description: Production pushes that need a go/no-go. The third subject of [[table:Showcase/Approvals]] `Of`, and a member of the [[table:Showcase/Tags]] `Applied to` set so a deploy can wear the same `urgent` tag a task does.

tables.name: Approvals
tables.description:
**WHY:** a sign-off is one workflow whatever it signs off — `Of` points at an [[table:Showcase/Expenses]] row, a [[table:Showcase/Contracts]] row or a [[table:Showcase/Deploys]] row, and `Decision` carries the same Requested → Approved / Rejected lifecycle for all three. Case 4 of the polymorphic showcase ([[Feature#182]]). Without a target set each subject table would need its own approval workflow, and a board of "everything waiting on me" could not exist.

`Of` → Expenses | Contracts | Deploys, many-to-one. Group a board on `Decision` to see the mixed queue.

tables.name: Line Items
tables.description: **WHY NOT:** the counter-example. `Expense` is a plain paired relation to [[table:Showcase/Expenses]] — one target table, an inverse `Line items` on the far side — because the fields that matter here are computed *through* it: `Expense category` is a lookup and `Line total` on Expenses is a sum rollup. Lookups and rollups need a single far table to read a field from; the engine refuses them on a target set (*Lookup needs a single-target relation*). A target set here would also be wrong on meaning: a line item belongs to exactly one expense and nothing else. Case 6 of the polymorphic showcase ([[Feature#182]]).

tables.name: Tags
tables.description:
**WHY:** one label, many kinds of thing — `Applied to` is a **many-to-many** target set spanning [[table:Showcase/Tasks]], [[table:Showcase/Docs]], [[table:Showcase/Projects]], [[table:Showcase/Meetings]] and [[table:Showcase/Deploys]], so `urgent` can sit on a task and a deploy in the same cell. Case 5 of the polymorphic showcase ([[Feature#182]]): the cell shows the first chips and a **+N** overflow, and the picker searches every member table at once.

A per-table tag field would need five multiselects kept in step by hand; here it is one field and one picker.

tables.name: Activity
tables.description:
**WHY:** an audit log points at *whatever changed* — `Subject` is one field whose target set is every table in this space, so the log stays one table with one timeline instead of a per-table history. Case 2 of the polymorphic showcase ([[Feature#182]]); this is how weave's own activity feed and the [[table:Workspace/Tables]] registry think.

`Subject` → every Showcase table, many-to-one. Sort by `When` for the timeline; the home badge on each chip says which table the change landed in.

description: Companies, the people at them, the deals in flight and every call, email and meeting along the way. Start at Companies: one row per organisation, Type is the relationship. Add Contacts under a company, open one Deal per opportunity and move its Stage, and log each touch as an Activity against the contact and the deal it served. Deal value on a company, Last touch on a contact and Weighted on a deal compute themselves; never type them. Search a table by Name before adding a row; the name is the identity.

tables.name: Companies
tables.description: One row per organisation you sell to, buy from or partner with. Search by Name before adding one. Type is the relationship (Prospect, Customer, Partner, Vendor, Ecosystem), never the industry. Deal value sums every deal on the company and needs no entry. Put what the company does in Description; conversations go on Activities, not here.

fields.name: Type
fields.description: The relationship: Prospect (you are pursuing them), Customer (they pay you), Partner (they sell with you), Vendor (you pay them), Ecosystem (adjacent, none of the above). One value. A competitor is Ecosystem.

fields.name: Industry
fields.description: The sector the company sells into. Pick the nearest; Other when none fits.

fields.name: Size
fields.description: Headcount band.

fields.name: Website
fields.description: Home page URL with its scheme, as https://example.com.

fields.name: City
fields.description: Headquarters city, plain text.

fields.name: Contacts
fields.description: The people at this company. Add a person from the Contacts table with Company set to this row.

fields.name: Deals
fields.description: Opportunities with this company. Add one from the Deals table with Company set to this row.

fields.name: Deal value
fields.description: Sum of Value across the company's Deals at every stage. Computed; do not set.

tables.name: Contacts
tables.description: The people at each company, one row each, linked to their Company. Role says what they decide on a deal. Last touch is the newest Activity date and fills itself. Log calls and emails as Activities on the contact, not in its Description.

fields.name: Title
fields.description: Job title as the person writes it.

fields.name: Company
fields.description: The one company the person works at. Move them when they change jobs.

fields.name: Role
fields.description: Part in the buying decision. Decision maker signs; Champion sells inside; Influencer shapes the choice; User works with the product; Gatekeeper controls access or budget.

fields.name: Email
fields.description: Work email, one address.

fields.name: Phone
fields.description: Digits with the country code, as +1 206 555 0100.

fields.name: Last touch
fields.description: Date of the newest Activity on this contact. Computed; do not set.

fields.name: Deals
fields.description: Deals this person is involved in. Set from the deal's Contacts field.

fields.name: Activities
fields.description: Every touch logged on this person, newest first.

tables.name: Deals
tables.description: One row per opportunity, linked to its Company and the Contacts on the buying side. Stage is the pipeline: Lead (not yet qualified), Qualified (need, budget and timing confirmed), Proposal (a proposal is out), Negotiation (terms in play), Won (signed), Lost (closed without a sale). Value is the total contract amount in USD, Probability your estimate as a fraction, Weighted their product. Keep Next step to one concrete action. The Pipeline view shows open deals, Won the closed ones. Notes holds the running narrative.

fields.name: Stage
fields.description: Pipeline position. Lead: unqualified. Qualified: need, budget and timing confirmed. Proposal: a proposal is out. Negotiation: terms in play. Won: signed. Lost: closed without a sale. Move one step at a time and log the Activity that caused the move.

fields.name: Company
fields.description: The buying organisation. One per deal.

fields.name: Value
fields.description: Total contract value in USD for the whole deal, never a monthly figure.

fields.name: Probability
fields.description: Chance of winning as a fraction between 0 and 1; 0.6 shows as 60%.

fields.name: Weighted
fields.description: Value times Probability. Computed; do not set.

fields.name: Close date
fields.description: The date the decision is expected. Move it when it slips rather than leaving it in the past.

fields.name: Contacts
fields.description: The people on the buying side, the Decision maker included.

fields.name: Source
fields.description: The deal's origin: Inbound (they reached out), Outbound (you reached out), Referral (a person introduced you), Partner (a partner company brought it), Event.

fields.name: Next step
fields.description: The single next action: who does what by when. Rewrite it after every activity. Blank means the deal is stalled.

fields.name: Activities
fields.description: Touches logged against this deal, newest first.

fields.name: Notes
fields.description: The running narrative: context, objections, decisions. Dated entries, newest first.

tables.name: Activities
tables.description: Every call, email, meeting, note and task, one row each, dated and linked to the Contact and the Deal it served. Kind says which. Done marks a touch that happened or a task finished; an unchecked Task with a Date is the to-do list (see the Tasks view). Name is a short subject, Notes holds what was said and agreed, Transcript holds the full text of a call or meeting. Company fills from the contact.

fields.name: Kind
fields.description: Call, Email or Meeting for a touch with the contact; Note for something learned with no contact event; Task for something to do by Date.

fields.name: Date
fields.description: The day it happened, or for a Task, the day it is due. ISO date.

fields.name: Contact
fields.description: The person on the other side. Required for a Call, Email or Meeting.

fields.name: Company
fields.description: The contact's company. Computed; do not set.

fields.name: Deal
fields.description: The opportunity this served. Leave empty for a touch with no deal.

fields.name: Done
fields.description: Checked when the touch happened or the task is finished. An unchecked Task is open.

fields.name: Notes
fields.description: Your summary of the exchange: decisions and follow-ups first, then the rest.

fields.name: Transcript
fields.description: The full text of a call or meeting, pasted whole. Summarise it in Notes.
